finding: The scene derives each label from a source agent id, but line 77 registers the labels with add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects(labels). The rendered labels therefore lose their world-space attachment to the corresponding node and collapse into a small central overlay band; at 854x480 they visibly overlap in the 3s, 5s, 8s and 11s samples. This weakens the film's claim that each visible worker is a source-bound object.

keep_unchanged: node and label position calculation at lines 65-68
canonical manifest and all production files for this proposal
candidate_change.why: Fixed-orientation labels remain readable toward the camera while staying in the same 3D coordinate system as their node. This is one atomic registration change: it restores node-to-label spatial continuity without adding unsupported identity data.

evidence.observation: The label text is deterministically derived from agent['id'], positioned from pos, collected into labels, then attached as fixed-in-frame objects.
The snapshot contains 15 selected agents (13 working, 2 idle); the rendered scene uses the same agents list and aggregate counts.
All samples show the worker labels in a central horizontal band with visible collisions/low separation while the nodes remain distributed around WORLD.

falsifier: Reject this candidate if a fresh render with the same manifest and camera still places labels in one central band, or if any of the 15 source agents cannot be matched one-to-one with a nearby visible label in at least two of the four sampled timestamps. Also reject it if fixed-orientation rendering makes labels unreadable at 854x480.
